mainTopic: רבי שמעון's unresolved view on a קומץ taken for a זבח; the sources for why מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות are invalid שלא לשמה, and why an אשם is not; and רב's rule about the מנחת העומר.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of רב הושעיא's question to רב אסי: what would רבי שמעון say if the קומץ of a מנחה was taken with the intent of an animal offering? רב אסי answers that no one knows רבי שמעון's real reasoning. The גמרא explains that the earlier explanations of רבה, רבא and רב אשי had each been challenged, so none could settle the question. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה and asks why מנחת קנאות is invalid שלא לשמה. רב נחמן first links it to a חטאת through the shared word עון. After a back-and-forth about whether the אשם would then be invalid too, the גמרא limits that link to leftover money (מותר נדבה). The real source for both מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות turns out to be the word ״היא״, as with a חטאת. The ״הוא״ written about an אשם teaches something else: an אשם stays an אשם until בית דין sends it out to graze. Finally רב rules that a מנחת העומר done שלא לשמה is פסולה, because it came to permit the new grain and failed, and he begins to apply this to the אשם נזיר, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון hold here? First possibility
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא asks what רבי שמעון would say about a קומץ taken for the sake of a זבח. First option: his reason is that obviously-false intent does not disqualify, and this case is also obviously false.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would רבי שמעון say about this? Maybe his reason is that a wrong intention that is obviously wrong does not make the offering invalid. If so, this case is also an obviously wrong intention, so it should be valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא asks רב אסי how רבי שמעון would rule when the קומץ of a מנחה is taken with the intent of an animal offering. He starts by offering the first possible reason behind רבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a מנחה offered for the sake of another מנחה stays valid. If the reason is that the wrong intent is obvious (מחשבה דמינכרא), then intending a flour offering as an animal offering is even more obviously false. So this case should also be valid.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason behind a ruling
intention, here a wrong intention during the offering
that is recognizable, meaning plainly visible as false
disqualifies the offering
the handful of flour removed from a מנחה and burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of the question. The case being asked about is a קומץ taken from a מנחה for the sake of a זבח (an animal offering), not for the sake of another מנחה.

phrases.english: What should I understand that Rabbi Shimon says?
phrases.notes: רב הושעיא is asking רב אסי about a קומץ taken from a מנחה for the sake of an animal offering.

phrases.english: Is the reason of Rabbi Shimon
because an intention that is recognizably false
does not disqualify?
And this too is a recognizably false intention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב הושעיא's question, which begins just before this text.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי שמעון would treat a מנחה whose קומץ was taken for the sake of a זבח as valid or invalid.

steps.title: Second possibility: the reason is the פסוק about the מנחה
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe רבי שמעון's reason is the פסוק "וזאת תורת המנחה", which makes all מנחות one law. That פסוק does not mention a זבח, so this case would be invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe רבי שמעון's reason is that the תורה says "This is the law of the מנחה", which makes all flour offerings one. It does not say "and the animal offering", so this case would be invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא gives the second side of his question: a different possible reason for רבי שמעון that would lead to the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון's source is "וזאת תורת המנחה", that פסוק only joins מנחות to each other. Mixing up one מנחה with another is fine, but intending a זבח falls outside the פסוק, so the מנחה would be invalid. The two possible reasons therefore give opposite rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: or perhaps; introduces the other side of a question
the law of the מנחה; read as one law for all flour offerings
an animal offering

phrases.english: Or perhaps the reason of Rabbi Shimon
is because it is written:
"And this is the law of the meal offering,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:7

phrases.english: and "animal offering" is not written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the question started in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי שמעון's reason is a פסוק that would make this case invalid.

steps.title: רב אסי: we do not know רבי שמעון's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי answers that no one has figured out the full depth of רבי שמעון's thinking, so the question stays unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said to him: Have we really understood רבי שמעון's thinking all the way through? No, we have not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי replies to רב הושעיא. He does not choose either side; he says we simply do not know רבי שמעון's real reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is really an admission that the question cannot be settled. Since the result depends on רבי שמעון's reason, and that reason is unknown, the case of a קומץ taken for a זבח stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: have we at all reached? (expects the answer 'no')
the full depth of his thinking

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב אסי is answering רב הושעיא.

phrases.english: Have we at all reached
the depth of the opinion of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם הִגַּעְנוּ לְסוֹף דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question of steps 1 and 2 by saying it cannot be decided.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer is possible, because רבי שמעון's reasoning is not known.

steps.title: Why רב אסי did not answer like רבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב אסי could not use רבה's explanation of רבי שמעון, because אביי had already challenged it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not answer him the way רבה explained it, because of אביי's question against רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks itself why רב אסי did not simply use an explanation said earlier. It answers that רבה's explanation was already challenged by אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה had explained רבי שמעון earlier on the דף. אביי raised a strong question against that explanation, so it could not be relied on to settle רב הושעיא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: he did not answer him; did not resolve the question for him
a difficulty or challenge against a view

phrases.english: He did not answer him in line with Rabba,
phrases.notes: רבה's explanation of רבי שמעון, and אביי's question on it, came earlier on this דף.

phrases.english: because of Abaye's difficulty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the answer in step 3 did not rely on an earlier explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out רבה's explanation as a way to settle the question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי had already raised a challenge against רבה's explanation.

steps.title: Why רב אסי did not answer like רבא
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי also could not use רבא's explanation based on "וזאת תורת המנחה". The same kind of פסוק, "וזאת תורת החטאת", appears for the חטאת, and there it does not make a change from one חטאת to another valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He also did not answer the way רבא explained it, because of the question from the פסוק "This is the law of the חטאת".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא's explanation also could not be used to answer רב הושעיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said רבי שמעון learns from "וזאת תורת המנחה" that all מנחות are one law. But the תורה uses the same wording for the חטאת, and a חטאת offered for the sake of another חטאת is still invalid. So that wording cannot be the real reason, and רבא's explanation is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: the law of the sin offering; a פסוק worded like "תורת המנחה"
sin offering

phrases.english: He did not answer him in line with Rava,
because of the difficulty from
"And this is the law of the sin offering."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:18. The same wording is used for the חטאת, yet a חטאת offered for another חטאת is still invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 4; rules out the second earlier explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out רבא's explanation based on "וזאת תורת המנחה".
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same wording for the חטאת does not make a change from one חטאת to another valid, so the wording cannot prove רבי שמעון's rule.

steps.title: רב אשי's explanation could not be used either
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי did not answer the question using רב אשי's explanation, because רב אחא בריה דרבא had already challenged it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי did not answer the question using רב אשי's explanation, because of the challenge raised by רב אחא בריה דרבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why רב אסי said no one fully understands רבי שמעון. The last available explanation, from רב אשי, also had a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 4 and 5 ruled out the explanations of רבה and רבא. Now רב אשי's explanation is ruled out too, because רב אחא בריה דרבא challenged it. With all three explanations gone, it makes sense that רב אסי could not answer רב הושעיא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: answers or resolves a question
a difficulty or challenge

steps.whatToRemember: All three explanations of רבי שמעון (רבה, רבא, רב אשי) had problems. That is why רב אסי said no one has figured out the full depth of רבי שמעון's thinking.

phrases.english: He did not answer him according to Rav Ashi,
phrases.notes: רב אשי's explanation came earlier on the דף.

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם קוּשְׁיָא דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא.
phrases.english: because of the difficulty raised by Rav Acha, son of Rava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final item in the list of explanations רב אסי could not use, after those of רבה and רבא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rules out רב אשי's explanation of רבי שמעון as a way to answer רב הושעיא's question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב אחא בריה דרבא had already challenged רב אשי's explanation.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the meal offering of jealousy is an exception?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exceptions. For מנחת חוטא the source is clear, because the תורה calls it a חטאת. It then asks for the source for מנחת קנאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: except for the meal offering of a sinner and the meal offering of jealousy. The meal offering of a sinner makes sense, because the תורה calls it a sin offering: "He shall not put oil on it and shall not put frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering." But for the meal offering of jealousy, how do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. It quotes the two exceptions and asks where we learn the second one, מנחת קנאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said most מנחות stay valid even when the קומץ is taken for another purpose, except these two. For מנחת חוטא there is a direct פסוק: the Torah calls it a חטאת, and a חטאת is invalid שלא לשמה. No פסוק calls מנחת קנאות a חטאת, so the גמרא asks for its source.

keyTerms.meaning: the meal offering brought by a poor sinner in place of an animal sin offering
the meal offering of jealousy, brought in the סוטה process
'granted' / 'this one makes sense', setting up a contrast with a harder case
'the Merciful One', meaning the Torah
'from where do we know?', asking for a source

phrases.english: Except for the meal offering of a sinner
and the meal offering of jealousy.
Granted, the meal offering of a sinner:
the Torah calls it a "sin offering,"
"He shall not put oil on it
and he shall not put frankincense on it
for it is a sin offering, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:11

phrases.english: But the meal offering of jealousy, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The גמרא leaves the רבי שמעון discussion and returns to the משנה's list of exceptions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that a מנחת קנאות is invalid when its קומץ is taken שלא לשמה.

steps.title: A teaching about the jealousy offering's leftover money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא taught before רב נחמן: the leftover money of a מנחת קנאות goes to נדבה offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught in front of רב נחמן: a meal offering of jealousy, its leftover money goes to voluntary offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer with a ברייתא that does not seem to be about our question at all. This step sets up the next one, where רב נחמן explains the reason behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats a מנחת קנאות the way we treat a חטאת: leftover money goes to communal נדבה offerings. The reason, given in the next step, will connect the two offerings in a way that also teaches the rule of שלא לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: here, a person who recited ברייתות from memory in the study hall
its leftover, here the money left after buying the offering
voluntary offerings, here communal offerings bought with the leftover money

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about leftover money, not about taking the קומץ for the wrong purpose. It matters because of the reason behind it, which comes in the next step.

phrases.english: For a tanna taught in front of Rav Nachman:
A meal offering of jealousy: its leftover goes to voluntary offerings.
phrases.notes: He means the money set aside for it. Whatever is left after buying the offering is used for communal gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא that treats a מנחת קנאות like a חטאת for leftover money, setting up the link explained in the next step.

steps.title: The shared word "iniquity" links the jealousy offering to a sin offering
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן agrees with the ברייתא. He explains that both offerings are described with the word עון, so a מנחת קנאות is like a חטאת: its leftover goes to נדבה, and it is invalid שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: You are right. About the meal offering of jealousy it says "bringing iniquity to remembrance," and about a sin offering it says "He gave it to you to bear the iniquity of the congregation." Just as a sin offering's leftover goes to voluntary offerings, so too the meal offering of jealousy's leftover goes to voluntary offerings. It is also like a sin offering in this: just as a sin offering is invalid if not offered for its own sake, so too the meal offering of jealousy is invalid if not for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the reason behind the ברייתא: the word עון appears with both offerings. That shared word also answers the question of step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because both offerings are described with the word עון, they are linked by a גזירה שוה. This link does more than explain the leftover money. It also makes a מנחת קנאות like a חטאת for the rule of שלא לשמה. That is the source for the משנה's second exception.

keyTerms.meaning: 'you are saying well', approving what was just said
'bringing iniquity to remembrance', the Torah's description of the מנחת קנאות
a link between two topics based on a shared word in the Torah
not for its own sake, offered with intent for a different offering

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן links a מנחת קנאות to a חטאת through the word עון, for both מותר נדבה and פסול שלא לשמה. Watch this: in step 14 the גמרא limits the link to מותר נדבה only, and in step 18 it finds a different source for the שלא לשמה rule (the word ״היא״).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first source offered for the משנה's second exception. The next steps challenge it, and the גמרא ends up keeping the link only for leftover money.

phrases.english: He said to him: You are saying well,
"bringing iniquity to remembrance" is written about it,
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:15

phrases.english: and about a sin offering it is written:
"And He gave it to you
to bear the iniquity of the congregation,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:17. The shared word עון is what connects the two offerings.

phrases.english: just as a sin offering, its leftover goes to voluntary offerings,
so too a meal offering of jealousy, its leftover goes to voluntary offerings.
And it is like a sin offering:
just as a sin offering is invalid if not offered for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת פְּסוּלָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ.
phrases.english: so too a meal offering of jealousy is invalid if not for its own sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the ברייתא from step 8 and uses that reason to answer the question of step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That a מנחת קנאות is invalid when its קומץ is taken שלא לשמה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word עון: "מזכרת עון" (במדבר 5:15) and "לשאת את עון העדה" (ויקרא 10:17).

steps.title: Then the אשם should also be invalid שלא לשמה
steps.stepSummary: If the word עון links מנחת קנאות to חטאת, it should also link אשם to חטאת, so an אשם would be invalid שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if that is so, an אשם should be invalid when it is not brought for its own sake, because it can learn from חטאת through the shared word 'עון'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן's method. The same word עון also appears by the אשם, so his link should make the אשם invalid שלא לשמה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן made מנחת קנאות like a חטאת because both use the word עון. But the פסוק about the אשם also says עון. The accepted halacha is that an אשם brought שלא לשמו is still valid, so a method that makes it invalid seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: But if that is so: introduces a result of the previous idea that seems wrong
Guilt offering
Not for its own sake, brought with the wrong intention
Learns, derives one law from another
Iniquity, sin: the shared word used for the link

phrases.english: But if that is so,
an אשם should be invalid when brought not for its own sake,
since it learns 'עון' 'עון' from חטאת.
phrases.notes: The word עון appears by the חטאת (ויקרא 10:17) and by the אשם (ויקרא 5:17).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's עון-עון link from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's link between מנחת קנאות and חטאת through the word עון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same link would also make the אשם invalid שלא לשמו, which goes against the accepted halacha that an אשם stays valid. So the link proves too much.

steps.title: 'עון' is not the same as 'עונו'
steps.stepSummary: A link is made only between identical words. The אשם says 'עונו', so it cannot learn from 'עון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'עון' from 'עון', but we do not learn 'עונו' from 'עון'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The אשם's פסוק uses a slightly different word, 'עונו' (his iniquity), so it cannot be linked to the חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on the exact wording. מנחת קנאות and חטאת both use plain 'עון', so they can be linked. The אשם has 'עונו', which is not an exact match, so it stays out of the link and remains valid שלא לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: We derive, we learn one case from another
His iniquity: the form of the word used by the אשם

phrases.english: We learn 'עון' from 'עון',
but we do not learn 'עונו' from 'עון'.
phrases.notes: The אשם פסוק says 'וְנָשָׂא עֲוֹנוֹ', 'he shall bear his iniquity', with an extra letter at the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the אשם also uses the word עון, it should be linked to חטאת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only identical words are linked. 'עונו' does not match 'עון', so the אשם is not included.

steps.title: A small wording difference does not stop a link
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל linked two completely different words, 'שב' and 'בא', so a one-letter difference should not matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'And the כהן shall return' and 'And the כהן shall come' are linked, because returning and coming mean the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the answer of step 11. It shows from a ברייתא that a link can be made even between different words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The school of רבי ישמעאל linked 'ושב' and 'ובא' in the laws of צרעת on a house, even though they are different words. If such different words can be linked, then 'עון' and 'עונו', which differ by only one letter, should surely be linkable. So the challenge about the אשם comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: What difference does it make?
Returning
Coming

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this is about צרעת for its own sake. The גמרא brings that case only to show how close two words must be for a link.

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
But the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
'And the כהן shall return,' 'And the כהן shall come' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:39 and 14:44, both about a house with צרעת.

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא שִׁיבָה זוֹ הִיא בִּיאָה.
phrases.english: this is returning, this is coming.
phrases.notes: He means the two words count as the same for the link, even though they are different words.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? וְהָא תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction between עון and עונו made in step 11.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A link does not need identical words. Even 'שב' and 'בא' were linked, so a one-letter difference cannot block it.

steps.title: The אשם could learn 'עונו' from שמיעת הקול
steps.stepSummary: Even if exact words are needed, the אשם's 'עונו' matches the 'עונו' said about the חטאת of שמיעת הקול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, let the אשם learn 'עונו' from 'עונו' of the sin of hearing the voice, as it is written: 'If he does not tell, he shall bear his iniquity.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second challenge. Even if we accept that only exact words can be linked, there is a חטאת that uses the exact same word 'עונו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן for שמיעת הקול is brought by someone who swore falsely that he knows no testimony. It is a kind of חטאת, and its פסוק says 'ונשא עונו'. That is an exact match to the אשם's 'עונו', so the אשם should still become invalid שלא לשמה, and the problem stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: adds another challenge
Let it learn
Hearing the voice: the case of one who swore falsely that he has no testimony to give

steps.whatToRemember: Both challenges (steps 12 and 13) knock down the 'עון vs. עונו' answer. The next step gives the real answer: the word-link teaches only about leftover money.

phrases.english: And furthermore, let it learn 'עונו' 'עונו'
from the sin of hearing the voice,
phrases.notes: This is someone who was asked to testify and swore he knew nothing; his קרבן is a חטאת.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'If he does not tell, he shall bear his iniquity.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger challenge to the answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 11, that the אשם cannot be linked to a חטאת because its word is 'עונו'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a חטאת, the one of שמיעת הקול, that also says 'עונו'. So even with an exact match the link works, and the אשם would be invalid שלא לשמה.

steps.title: The word-link teaches only about leftover money
steps.stepSummary: The גזירה שוה from the word עון was learned only for מותר נדבה, not for the פסול of שלא לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when they learned the word-link, they learned it only for the rule that leftover money goes to voluntary offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the אשם. It shrinks what the word-link teaches: it only tells us that leftover money goes to נדבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 argued that if the word-link makes an offering פסול שלא לשמה, an אשם should be פסול too, and steps 12–13 kept that challenge alive. Now the link no longer teaches anything about שלא לשמה. So the אשם problem disappears. It only shares the 'leftover goes to נדבה' rule, which causes no difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two places in the תורה that share the same word, so a law in one applies to the other
Leftover money set aside for an offering that was not used
Voluntary offerings bought from leftover money

phrases.english: Rather, when they derived the verbal analogy,
it was for the surplus going to gift offerings that they derived it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 12–13 rejected the עון/עונו distinction, this gives a new answer to the אשם challenge of step 10 by limiting what the גזירה שוה teaches
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word-link of עון teaches both מותר נדבה and פסול שלא לשמה, so the אשם would be פסול שלא לשמה
steps.terutzMaskana: The word-link teaches only מותר נדבה, so the אשם is not affected

steps.title: Objection: a word-link cannot be used halfway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא anticipates an objection: there is a rule that a גזירה שוה cannot be applied only partly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: there is no half word-link.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible objection to its own answer. It sets up the reply that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גזירה שוה carries over all the laws, not just some of them. So limiting it to מותר נדבה alone seems to break that rule. The גמרא will now show why this case is different.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule that a word-link cannot be used for only part of the laws
'And if you will say'; the גמרא heading off a possible objection

phrases.english: And if you would say:
there is no partial verbal analogy –

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא: אֵין גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה לְמֶחֱצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Anticipates an objection to the answer in Step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 14 that the גזירה שוה teaches only מותר נדבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A גזירה שוה must carry over all its laws. Taking just one law from it is not allowed.

steps.title: The תורה limited the שלא לשמה rule to a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק ״ושחט אותה לחטאת״ shows that only a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה. All other offerings are valid either way, so the word-link cannot carry that law.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה revealed about a חטאת: 'And he shall slaughter it for a חטאת.' 'It' is valid for its own sake and invalid not for its own sake. But all other offerings, whether for their own sake or not, are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection. A פסוק itself shows that the פסול of שלא לשמה belongs only to a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אותה ('it') limits the rule to the חטאת alone. Because the תורה blocked this law from spreading, the word-link has nothing to carry over except מותר נדבה. That is not a forbidden 'half' link. The תורה itself removed the other half.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One revealed'; the תורה made it clear in a פסוק
Offered for its own purpose, as the offering it really is
Offered with the intent that it be a different kind of offering
Valid offerings

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule that a wrong intention ruins only certain offerings. Most קדשים stay valid even when offered שלא לשמן.

phrases.english: the Merciful One revealed regarding a sin offering,
“And he shall slaughter it for a sin offering” –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:33

phrases.english: it, for its own sake, is valid,
not for its own sake, it is disqualified.
But all other sacrificial offerings,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִשְׁמָן בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן – כְּשֵׁרִים.
phrases.english: whether for their sake or not for their sake – are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק blocks part of the derivation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Limiting the word-link to מותר נדבה breaks the rule against a half גזירה שוה
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק ״אותה״ limits פסול שלא לשמה to a חטאת, so the link can only teach מותר נדבה

steps.title: Then where do we learn the two מנחות are invalid?
steps.stepSummary: If only a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה, where do we learn that מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות are also פסול שלא לשמן?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, the sinner's meal offering and the meal offering of jealousy, which are invalid not for their own sake, from where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. If the תורה limited the rule to a חטאת, we need a source for these two מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות are פסול when the קמיצה is done שלא לשמן. But Step 16 said all offerings besides a חטאת are valid. So the גמרא needs a new source for these two.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering brought by a poor sinner in place of an animal חטאת
The barley offering brought for a סוטה, a woman suspected by her husband
'From where do we know this?'; asking for a source

phrases.english: But then, the meal offering of a sinner and the meal offering of jealousy,
which are disqualified not for their sake – from where do we derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִנְחַת חוֹטֵא וּמִנְחַת קְנָאוֹת דִּפְסוּלִין שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the consequence of Step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה rules that these two מנחות are פסול שלא לשמן. If the פסוק limits the rule to a חטאת, they are left with no source.

steps.title: The word ״היא״ is written about them too
steps.stepSummary: A חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה because of the word ״היא״. The same word appears about both מנחות, so they share the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חטאת, what is the reason? Because 'it is' is written about it. So too, 'it is' is written about them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source. The word ״היא״ ('it is') that makes a חטאת פסול שלא לשמה is also written about these two מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״היא״ means the offering is valid only as exactly what it is. This word does not come from the general word-link. It appears directly in the פסוקים about מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות, so they get the same פסול. The אשם does not have this word in the same way, so it stays out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the reason?'
'It is'; a word that limits the offering to being exactly what it is
'So too'; the same reasoning applies here

steps.whatToRemember: The word-link of עון teaches only מותר נדבה. The פסול of שלא לשמה for מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות comes from the word ״היא״, just as it does for a חטאת.

phrases.english: A sin offering – what is the reason?
Because “it is” is written about it,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 4:24

phrases.english: so too, “it is” is written about them.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:11 for the sinner's מנחה, and במדבר 5:15 for the מנחת קנאות.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַטָּאת טַעְמָא מַאי, מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב בַּהּ ״הִיא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Providing an independent source from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the word-link, nothing makes these מנחות פסול שלא לשמן
steps.terutzMaskana: The word ״היא″ written about them makes them פסול שלא לשמן, just like a חטאת

steps.title: The word ״הוא״ also appears about an אשם
steps.stepSummary: If ״היא״ makes a חטאת פסול שלא לשמה, then ״הוא״ written about an אשם should make the אשם פסול שלא לשמו too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an אשם too — it says ״הוא״ about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 18. The same kind of word, ״הוא״, is written about an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 said the word ״היא״ is the source that a חטאת is פסול שלא לשמה. The פסוק ״אשם הוא״ uses the same kind of word, so by that logic an אשם should also be פסול. But the halacha is that an אשם is valid even when brought שלא לשמו.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering
"It" (masculine), the word in the פסוק ״אשם הוא״
But it is written about it!

phrases.english: A guilt offering too —
isn't "it" written about it?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:5, "אשם הוא" — "it is a guilt offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in step 18 by applying it to the אשם.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ״היא״ is what makes a קרבן פסול שלא לשמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the word works for a חטאת, the same word about an אשם should give the same result, which does not match the halacha.

steps.title: The ״הוא״ of אשם comes after the burning of the fats
steps.stepSummary: The ״הוא״ about an אשם is written after the פסוק describes burning the אימורין, so it does not make the offering פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ״הוא״ is written after the burning of the sacrificial parts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ״הוא״ of an אשם is written in a different place in the פסוק than the ״היא״ of a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא 7:5, ״אשם הוא״ comes right after the instruction to burn the אימורין on the מזבח. So the word is tied to that late stage of the עבודה, not to the main עבודות like שחיטה. The next step explains why this matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning parts of a קרבן on the מזבח
The fats and parts of a קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: That "it"
after the burning of the sacrificial parts
is where it is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא ״הוּא״ לְאַחַר הַקְטָרַת אֵימוּרִין הוּא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the placement of the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״הוא״ by אשם works like ״היא״ by חטאת and makes it פסול שלא לשמו.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ״הוא״ of אשם refers to the stage after the burning of the אימורין, so it cannot make the אשם פסול.

steps.title: A ברייתא backs up the answer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing. An אשם is valid even if its אימורין were never burned, so a ״הוא״ written about that stage cannot make it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: But about an אשם, ״הוא״ is only said after the burning of the sacrificial parts. And the אשם itself is valid even if its parts were not burned at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning the אימורין is not needed for the קרבן to be valid. An אשם whose fats were never burned is still כשר. If skipping the burning altogether does not ruin it, then doing the burning שלא לשמו surely cannot ruin it. So the ״הוא״ written about that stage cannot be a source for פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Valid; the קרבן counts
The offering itself

steps.whatToRemember: An אשם is not פסול שלא לשמו. Its ״הוא״ is written about the burning of the fats, and that burning is not even needed for the קרבן to be valid.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
But about a guilt offering, "it" is not said
except after the burning of the sacrificial parts,

phrases.aramaic: הוּא עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא הוּקְטְרוּ אֵימוּרָיו כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: and the offering itself, if its parts were not burned, is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: אֲבָל אָשָׁם לֹא נֶאֱמַר בּוֹ ״הוּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 20's answer with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the ״הוא״ of אשם does not make it פסול שלא לשמו
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the ״הוא״ comes after the burning, and that an אשם is valid even without the burning

steps.title: So what is the word ״הוא״ there for?
steps.stepSummary: If ״הוא״ does not make an אשם פסול שלא לשמו, why did the תורה write it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then why do I need ״הוא״?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks what the extra word ״הוא״ by אשם comes to teach. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word in the תורה is assumed to teach something. Once the גמרא has said that ״הוא״ is not a source for פסול שלא לשמו, it must find a different purpose for the word.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? What does it teach?

phrases.english: But then, why do I need "it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from steps 20–21: once the word is not used for פסול, its purpose is unclear.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word ״הוא״ in ״אשם הוא״ teaches

steps.title: רב הונא's ruling about an אשם sent out to graze
steps.stepSummary: The word is needed for רב הונא's ruling in the name of רב: an אשם that was sent out to graze and then slaughtered without a stated purpose is valid as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for what רב הונא said in the name of רב: An אשם that was sent out to graze, and someone slaughtered it without saying what it was for, is valid as an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 22. It brings רב הונא's ruling, and the next step shows how ״הוא״ is the source for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes an אשם can no longer be brought as an אשם, for example because its owner died. בית דין then sends it out to graze until it gets a מום, so it can be sold and the money used for an עולה. רב rules that if someone slaughtered it before that, without stating a purpose, it is valid as an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Sent out (by בית דין) to graze until it gets a מום
Without stating a purpose
As a burnt offering

phrases.english: For what רב הונא said in the name of רב:
A guilt offering that was sent out to graze,
phrases.notes: This happens when the אשם can't be brought as an אשם anymore, for example if its owner died.

phrases.english: and someone slaughtered it without stating a purpose —
it is valid as a burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְרַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: אָשָׁם שֶׁנִּיתַּק לִרְעִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״הוא״ is needed for רב הונא's ruling about an אשם that was ניתק לרעיה.

steps.title: ״הוא״ means the אשם stays what it is
steps.stepSummary: From רב's ruling we learn that only an אשם that was sent out to graze can count as an עולה. One that was not sent out stays an אשם, because ״הוא״ means it stays as it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it was sent out to graze, yes. If it was not sent out, no. The פסוק says ״הוא״ — it stays in its state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רב's words and then shows that the word ״הוא״ is the source for it. This finishes the answer to step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the ruling about an אשם that was ניתק לרעיה. That implies an אשם that was not sent out does not become an עולה. The reason is ״הוא״: the animal stays an אשם until בית דין changes its purpose. So ״הוא״ teaches that an אשם keeps its identity, not that it is פסול שלא לשמו.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes / no
It shall stay in its state, still an אשם

steps.whatToRemember: The ״הוא״ of אשם does not make it פסול שלא לשמו. It teaches that an אשם stays an אשם until בית דין sends it out to graze. Only then can it count as an עולה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two words. ״היא״ by חטאת (and the מנחות) is a source for פסול שלא לשמה. ״הוא״ by אשם teaches something else: the animal keeps its status as an אשם.

phrases.english: If it was sent out to graze — yes,
if it was not sent out — no.
phrases.notes: He means it is not valid as an עולה, because it is still an אשם.

phrases.english: The verse says: "It,"
it shall remain as it is.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיתַּק – אִין, לֹא נִיתַּק – לָא. אָמַר קְרָא: ״הוּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רב's ruling in step 23 and shows that ״הוא״ is its source, finishing the answer to step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That ״הוא״ is needed to teach that an אשם that was not ניתק לרעיה keeps its status
steps.raayaSupportSource: The inference from רב's ruling, together with the פסוק ״אשם הוא״

steps.title: רב: An עומר Offering Done for the Wrong Purpose Is Disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a מנחת העומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה is פסולה. Its job was to permit the new grain, and it failed to do that. He then starts to apply the same reasoning to the אשם נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: If the כהן took the handful from the עומר offering for the wrong purpose, it is disqualified. That offering came to permit something, and it did not permit it. You say the same thing about the guilt offering of a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב about the מנחת העומר, which is an exception to the משנה's rule that wrong-purpose מנחות stay כשרות. The last line starts to apply the same idea to the אשם נזיר, and the explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most מנחות done שלא לשמן are still כשרות; they just don't count for the owner. The עומר is different because it has one public job, permitting the new grain. If it fails at that job, nothing is left for it to accomplish, so רב says it is פסולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן. It permits eating the new year's grain.
The כהן's taking a handful from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח.
Done with the wrong purpose in mind, not for the offering it really is.
Since it came to permit. Its whole purpose is to make something allowed.
Grain of the new crop, which is forbidden to eat until the עומר is brought.
The guilt offering a נזיר who became טמא brings so he can restart his נזירות in purity.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב is arguing with the משנה. The משנה's rule that wrong-purpose מנחות are כשרות still holds for most מנחות. רב is pointing out a special exception, an offering whose whole job is to permit something.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a new principle: an offering that 'comes to permit' (בא להתיר) is פסול if done שלא לשמו, because then it does not do its job. The rest of the sugya will test and apply this idea.

phrases.english: Rav says:

phrases.aramaic: מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר שֶׁקְּמָצָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ – פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: An omer meal offering from which he removed a handful not for its own sake is disqualified,
since it came in order to permit
and it did not permit.
phrases.notes: The עומר's job is to permit eating the new grain. Done for the wrong purpose, it fails at that job.

phrases.english: And so you say with regard to the guilt offering of a nazirite

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מִנְחַת הָעוֹמֶר שֶׁקְּמָצָהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ״הוא״ discussion about the אשם has ended. The גמרא returns to the משנה's rule about מנחות done שלא לשמן and brings רב's exception for the עומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחת העומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה is פסולה, because it came to permit the new grain and did not. The same reasoning is beginning to be applied to the אשם נזיר.
